abstract: Algal-bacterial symbiotic and mutualistic systems enhance community stability and functional performance through interspecies cooperation and signal exchange, demonstrating considerable potential in environmental remediation and sustainable biomanufacturing. This review systematically summarizes the fundamental interaction types and underlying mechanisms of algal-bacterial symbiosis and mutualism, with a particular focus on enabling technologies for the rational reconstruction of engineered mutualistic consortia and their emerging applications in environmental remediation and biomanufacturing. Different interaction modes, including mutualism, commensalism, parasitism, and endosymbiosis, are comparatively discussed, together with key regulatory mechanisms such as chemical signaling, nutrient exchange, horizontal gene transfer, and homeostasis maintenance under abiotic stress conditions. At the technical level, this paper introduces the recent advances in single-cell dynamic monitoring approaches, artificial intelligence-driven design platforms, and synthetic community engineering strategies integrating both top-down and bottom-up methodologies. Furthermore, this paper discusses the potential applications of algal-bacterial mutualistic systems in wastewater remediation, aquaculture, bioenergy recovery, and sustainable bioproduction and points out the current research challenges related to mechanism understanding, species specificity, long-term system stability, and ecological risk assessment. Finally, this review proposes that interdisciplinary approaches integrating multi-omics analyses, computational modeling, and controllable environmental validation will facilitate the development of efficient, robust, and sustainable algal-bacterial symbiotic systems, thereby providing theoretical guidance and technical support for advancing synthetic biology-driven resource utilization and green biomanufacturing.

ChinaSheng Wu Gong Cheng Xue Bao94264631000-3061IMSymbiosisphysiologyBacterial Physiological PhenomenaBacteriametabolismEnvironmental Restoration and Remediation藻菌共生或互生体系通过种间协作与信号交流提升系统稳定性与功能表现，在环境修复与绿色制造领域展现出广阔的应用前景。本文从共生及互生体系的基本类型与作用机制出发，系统综述了人工互生系统理性重构的关键使能技术，并展望了其在环境修复、生物制造等方面的应用潜力。重点分析了互利共生、偏利共生、寄生及内共生等不同相互作用模式，探讨了化学信号传递、营养交换、基因水平转移及非生物胁迫下稳态维持等核心机制。在技术层面，介绍了基于单细胞行为动态监测的分析手段、人工智能驱动的设计平台，以及“自上而下”和“自下而上”策略相结合的合成菌群构建方法。进一步讨论了藻菌互生系统在水体修复、水产养殖、生物能源回收与绿色生产等方面的潜在应用，同时指出当前研究在机制解析、物种特异性、系统稳定性及生态风险等方面面临的挑战。最后提出，通过多组学整合、计算模拟与可控环境验证等跨学科策略，可推动藻菌共生系统向高效、稳定、可持续方向发展，为合成生物学在资源利用与生物制造中的深化应用提供理论参考与技术支撑。.algal-bacterial symbiosisartificial intelligenceenvironmental remediationgreen biomanufacturinginteraction mechanismsynthetic biology作者声明没有任何可能会影响本文所报告工作的已知经济利益或个人关系。202692353620269235352026923133ppublish4277365210.13345/j.cjb.2601331000-3061(2026)09-3884-21FIELD CB, BEHRENFELD MJ, RANDERSON JT, FALKOWSKI P.
